title: Sunlight is 8 minutes old
body: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth. When you look at the Sun, you see it as it was just over 8 minutes ago.

title: Boiling point and altitude
body: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level. Higher up, air pressure is lower, so water boils at a lower temperature. On top of Mount Everest it boils at roughly 70 °C, which is why cooking takes longer there.

title: 206 bones
body: An adult human skeleton usually has 206 bones. Babies are born with around 270, and many of them fuse together as the body grows.

title: The double helix
body: In 1953 James Watson and Francis Crick described DNA's double helix structure. Their model relied on X-ray images made by Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling.

title: How photosynthesis works
body: Plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose (sugar) and oxygen. It happens mainly in the leaves, inside chloroplasts, using the green pigment chlorophyll. Almost all oxygen we breathe comes from it.

title: The speed of light
body: Light travels through a vacuum at exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, about 300,000 km every second. Nothing carrying information can travel faster.

title: What causes tides
body: Tides are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity pulling on Earth's oceans, with a smaller effect from the Sun. Most coasts get two high tides and two low tides a day.

title: The biggest planet
body: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system. It is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined, and about 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

title: The hottest planet
body: Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun. Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping the surface around 465 °C, hot enough to melt lead.

title: Antibiotics and viruses
body: Antibiotics kill bacteria or stop them growing. They do not work against viruses such as colds and flu. Using them when they are not needed helps bacteria become resistant.

title: The discovery of penicillin
body: In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed that a mould, Penicillium, killed bacteria growing in a dish in his London lab. Penicillin became the first widely used antibiotic in the 1940s.

title: Why blood is red
body: Red blood cells are full of haemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that carries oxygen from the lungs to the body. The iron-based haem group gives blood its red colour.

title: The speed of sound
body: Sound travels through air at about 343 metres per second at 20 °C. It moves faster through water and even faster through solids like steel.

title: 118 elements
body: The periodic table has 118 confirmed chemical elements. The last four, including oganesson (element 118), were officially named in 2016.

title: Diamond and graphite
body: Diamond and graphite (the 'lead' in pencils) are both pure carbon. The only difference is how the carbon atoms are arranged, which makes one the hardest natural material and the other soft.

title: What air is made of
body: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and nearly 1% argon. Carbon dioxide is only about 0.04%, but it has a big effect on the climate.

title: 86 billion neurons
body: The human brain contains roughly 86 billion nerve cells (neurons), connected by trillions of synapses. It uses about 20% of the body's energy while making up only about 2% of body weight.

title: How vaccines work
body: A vaccine trains the immune system to recognise a germ, using a harmless part or weakened form of it. If the real germ arrives later, the body can fight it faster.

title: The cell's power plants
body: Mitochondria produce most of the chemical energy a cell uses, in the form of a molecule called ATP. They have their own small set of DNA, inherited from the mother.

title: Around Earth in 90 minutes
body: The International Space Station travels at about 28,000 km/h and circles Earth roughly every 90 minutes, so astronauts on board see about 16 sunrises a day.

title: Moore's law
body: In 1965 Gordon Moore observed that the number of transistors on a chip was doubling regularly; in 1975 he revised it to about every two years. This trend drove decades of faster, cheaper computers.

title: Absolute zero
body: Absolute zero, −273.15 °C (0 kelvin), is the lowest possible temperature, where particles have the least possible energy. Scientists have cooled matter to within billionths of a degree of it.

title: Newton's first law
body: An object stays still, or keeps moving in a straight line at the same speed, unless a force acts on it. This is inertia. It is why passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes suddenly.

title: A light-year is a distance
body: A light-year is how far light travels in one year: about 9.46 trillion km. It measures distance, not time. The nearest star after the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away.

title: Inside an atom
body: An atom has a tiny nucleus of protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge), surrounded by electrons (negative). The number of protons decides which element it is: 6 protons is always carbon.

title: The pH scale
body: pH measures how acidic or alkaline a liquid is, usually from 0 to 14. 7 is neutral (pure water). Below 7 is acidic, like lemon juice; above 7 is alkaline, like soap.

title: The greenhouse effect
body: Gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour let sunlight in but trap some of the heat Earth gives off. Without it, Earth would be far too cold for life; more of these gases warm the planet further.

title: Science word: catalyst
body: Meaning: a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up. Enzymes are catalysts in living things.
example_sentence: Enzymes in saliva act as a catalyst to break down starch.

title: Science word: osmosis
body: Meaning: the movement of water through a membrane from a weaker solution to a stronger one.
example_sentence: Plant roots take in water by osmosis.

title: Science word: hypothesis
body: Meaning: a proposed explanation that can be tested by experiment or observation.
example_sentence: Her hypothesis was that plants grow faster with music.

title: Light versus sound
body: Physics check.
explanation: Light moves at about 300,000 km per second; sound in air at about 0.34 km per second. That is why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

title: Counting bones
body: Human body check.
statement: An adult human usually has 206 bones
explanation: Adults usually have 206 bones. Babies have more, around 270, and many fuse as they grow.

title: Antibiotics and colds
body: Health check.
statement: Antibiotics cure viral infections like the common cold
explanation: Colds and flu are caused by viruses. Antibiotics only work on bacteria, and misusing them causes resistance.

title: Our Sun
body: Space check.
explanation: The Sun is a medium-sized star, a huge ball of hot gas powered by nuclear fusion.

title: Cooking on a mountain
body: Physics check.
statement: Water boils at a lower temperature high on a mountain
explanation: Lower air pressure at altitude lowers the boiling point. On Everest water boils at about 70 °C.

title: Hottest planet check
body: Space check.
statement: Mercury is the hottest planet in our solar system
explanation: Venus is hotter (about 465 °C) because its thick atmosphere traps heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

title: What diamonds are made of
body: Chemistry check.
explanation: Diamond is pure carbon with its atoms locked in a very strong 3D pattern.

title: The main gas in air
body: Earth science check.
statement: Oxygen is the most common gas in Earth's air
explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

title: Are bats birds?
body: Biology check.
explanation: Bats have fur, give birth to live young and feed them milk. They are the only mammals capable of true flight.

title: Lightning myths
body: Weather check.
statement: Lightning never strikes the same place twice
explanation: Tall structures are hit again and again. New York's Empire State Building is struck many times every year.
